en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Chattupāhanavagga 87.
The Training Rule on Women’s Ornaments.
At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs were wearing women’s ornaments.
People criticized, complained, and spread it about, saying:
“How can these bhikkhunīs wear women’s ornaments? They are just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures!”
The bhikkhunīs heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those bhikkhunīs who were few in desires... [and so on]... they grumbled, complained, and criticized:
"How can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six wear women's ornaments?"... [and so on]...
“Is it true, monks, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs wear women’s ornaments?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
“How indeed, monks, can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs wear women’s ornaments?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of the faithful...
And thus, monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule:”
“Whatever nun should wear women’s ornaments, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya). Regarding “whatever nun”:
whichever [nun], of whatever kind... [etc.]... [as per the standard formula].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Female ornament" means:
[The robe] reaches to the head, reaches to the neck, reaches to the hands, reaches to the feet, or reaches to the hips.
"Should wear it" means:
if she wears it even once, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
There is no offense for one who is ill,
or for one who is insane.
"Regarding the first offender":
thus concludes the fourth training rule.
